findings.title: Deferred retained-source selection for repeat publication (known limitation a)
findings.detail: The coordinator always renders the observed active surface. When an ArrTags Published session already exists, the active surface is the previous ArrTags output, so a repeat generation would derive from (and double-badge) that output instead of the retained original artifact (architecture section 9 step 4). This is safety-neutral in this task: the coordinator is not wired to any invoker (no event/queue/startup scan), the publisher reuses the retained session artifact and ownership/publication tokens, and the before-mutation revalidation still aborts on any external change. The architecture explicitly assigns retained-source selection and the invoking pipeline to Phase 6, and the worker report documents it. Not a 5.8 acceptance gap, but Phase 6 must gate repeat publication before this entry point is driven.

findings.title: A few defensive coordinator branches are untested
findings.detail: The 23 focused cases exercise every acceptance-relevant branch (published; absent source; four failed-read classes; pass-through including real-renderer NoMetadata/MatchNotEligible; render failure/exception; publication failure/blocked/cancelled; cancellation before and during read; invalid input; shared observation; source-changed abort). Not directly exercised: reader returning null, reader throwing a non-cancellation exception, publisher throwing an exception, the internal overload's non-present-observation rejection, and the TryCreateSourceImageInput false branch. These are single-path defensive guards and do not hide an acceptance gap, but explicit coverage would strengthen the gate.

findings.title: Preserved/Cancelled wording can overstate the guarantee after a mutation may have started
findings.detail: ArtworkGenerationResult.Preserved is defined as the inverse of Published, and ArtworkGenerationOutcome.Cancelled is documented as 'no partial artifact or publication occurred'. Publication outcomes such as cancellation during SaveImage or a readback mismatch can leave the external image in an uncertain state; task 5.7 reconciliation owns that uncertainty. This mirrors the pre-existing ArtworkPublicationOutcome convention and the preservation guarantee the task actually requires (absent/failed source, render pass-through, render failure, missing/ineligible metadata) is exact. Documentation nuance only.

findings.title: Request doc claims no filesystem path while embedded MediaIdentity can carry one
findings.detail: The ArtworkGenerationRequest summary states the request carries no path, but MediaIdentity.MediaLocation.PrimaryPath is a raw path that a caller may populate. This is the same pre-existing pattern as RenderRequest (both carry MediaIdentity). The result and persisted state do not carry that path, and the boundary test only inspects top-level property names/namespaces, so it would not catch a nested path. Consider narrowing the doc claim or asserting nested host-neutrality.

findings.title: Caller-supplied OperationalLimits only bound the renderer
findings.detail: The request's Limits are passed to RenderRequest and bound decode/output, but the source read and derived-artifact promotion use the DI-configured limits of the reader/publisher. This is the established task 5.3/5.5 design and is harmless for the preservation guarantee; worth documenting so callers do not assume request.Limits are fully authoritative.
